NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's gold ring scheme, which was scheduled to be launched on September 15, shall be deferred from its expected date. The announcement comes as the CM prepares for his first official overseas visit to London. Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.Vijay will leave Chennai for London via Dubai on Wednesday night and is expected to stay in the UK capital for a few days. He will travel on an Emirates Airlines passenger flight.During the visit, Vijay is expected to invite European companies to set up businesses in Tamil Nadu and seek fresh investment commitments for the state. Senior officials from the industries and finance departments are also expected to travel to London. Some may leave ahead of the chief minister to prepare for his meetings with prospective investors.The visit comes soon after the ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’, where the state government announced investment commitments worth Rs 1,02,514 crore through 104 memorandums of understanding (MoUs).Security and protocol arrangements for Vijay’s departure are also being finalised.A high-level Advance Security Liaison meeting is reportedly scheduled at Chennai’s old airport on Wednesday to review the arrangements.Vijay’s London visit also comes amid key political developments in Tamil Nadu. Before leaving for the UK, he is scheduled to chair a second alliance coordination meeting at the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam headquarters in Panaiyur.The meeting is expected to discuss the structure of the ruling alliance and post-poll coalition arrangements. A Common Minimum Programme is also on the agenda, along with discussions on a steering committee and an official name for the alliance.Invitations have reportedly been sent to all alliance partners, including Congress, VCK, IUML, MDMK, CPI and CPM. Congress, VCK, IUML and MDMK have confirmed their attendance, while the Left parties are likely to stay away.Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election. The initiative was planned as a symbolic gift to newborns and draws on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’.Under the scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.“Through this scheme, the government assumes the role of the maaman (uncle) for every child born in its institutions, presenting a gold ring as an enduring token of welcome,” a government order said.The scheme was originally scheduled to be launched on September 15, which coincides with the birth anniversary of former chief minister C N Annadurai.It will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday. The government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of the child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover all newborns delivered at government institutions. There will be no restriction based on birth order and no gender-based discrimination.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements. A project and programme management unit will also be established to oversee implementation and monitoring.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries each year, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or about 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The scheme is open to Tamil Nadu residents whose children are delivered at government institutions. Mothers will have to submit proof of residence, with documents such as ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates accepted.The government said the initiative was intended to combine cultural significance with public healthcare.“Gold carries profound cultural and emotional resonance in Tamil Nadu. Gifting gold to a newborn celebrates the baby’s arrival, honours the mother’s noble journey and transforms public health delivery into a source of immense community pride,” the order said.
Article Summary: Under Vijay's scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600. Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Serena Williams bought a 2.7-acre Bel-Air estate with a 6,101-sq-ft mansion; after repeated price cuts, it sold for $8.1 million after being listed for nearly $12 million
Article Text:
Serena Williams bought a 2.7-acre Bel-Air estate with a 6,101-sq-ft mansion; after repeated price cuts, it sold for $8.1 million after being listed for nearly $12 million

What did Serena Williams pay for her Bel-Air estate in 2006

Why did Serena Williams list the Bel-Air mansion for nearly $12 million

What was inside Serena Williams’ 6,101-square-foot Bel-Air mansion

not

How much did Serena Williams reduce the Bel-Air asking price

How much profit did Serena Williams make from the $8.1 million sale

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena Williams sold her long-held Bel-Air estate for $8.1 million in April 2019, ending a sale process that lasted about 18 months. The tennis star had bought the property in 2006 for $6.612 million and first listed it in late 2017 for $11.995 million, or nearly $12 million. The 1935-built home sits on about 2.7 acres and has 6,101 square feet of living space, six bedrooms and seven bathrooms. Williams later reduced the asking price to $9.995 million, but the property eventually changed hands for $8.1 million, giving her a gross gain over what she originally paid.Serena Williams bought the Bel-Air property in 2006 for $6.612 million, according to property records reported by The Washington Post. At the time, the home gave her a large private space in one of Los Angeles’ most well-known luxury neighborhoods.The house was built in 1935, so it was not a newly constructed celebrity mansion when Williams bought it. Instead, the property had an older California feel, with plenty of land around the main house. Its location in the Stone Canyon area also gave the estate a level of privacy that is difficult to find on a large residential property in Los Angeles.Williams kept the home for more than a decade. During those years, her life changed in major ways, both on and off the tennis court, while the Bel-Air house remained one of her main Los Angeles properties.Williams put the property on the market in late 2017 with an asking price of $11.995 million. The timing came after she welcomed her daughter, Olympia, in September 2017, and married Alexis Ohanian.Around the same period, Williams and Ohanian bought a newer home in the Beverly Hills area for about $6.7 million. That five-bedroom property was built with features aimed at modern family living, including a pool, wine cellar and yoga room.The move meant Williams no longer needed to keep the older Bel-Air estate as her main Los Angeles home. The Bel-Air house was much larger in terms of land, but the newer property offered a different kind of setup for the family.The initial $11.995 million price was also well above what Williams had paid for the house. At that figure, the estate was being offered for roughly $5.4 million more than its 2006 purchase price.The Bel-Air home had six bedrooms, seven bathrooms and about 6,101 square feet of living space. It was built across a large, tree-filled property, giving the house a more private setting than its street address might suggest.Inside, the home had marble and hardwood floors, high ceilings and a large living room. The living room included a curved wall of clerestory windows and French doors that opened toward the greenery outside. There was also a dark wood executive office or study and a wet bar.The main bedroom area was larger than a standard bedroom suite. It included a sitting area, dressing rooms and a large bathroom.One of the home’s more unusual features was a full-service hair salon. That stood out even among the property’s other luxury features and suited Williams’ busy life in tennis, fashion and public appearances.The estate also had a gym and a three-car garage. Outside, the grounds included a swimming pool, pool house, gardens, covered patio areas and private walking trails.Despite being owned by one of tennis’ greatest players, the property didhave a tennis court.The original $11.995 million asking price did not bring a sale quickly. After the property had spent months on the market, Williams cut the price by about $2 million in April 2018.The new asking price was $9.995 million. That was still nearly $3.4 million above the $6.612 million Williams had paid for the home in 2006, but it was a major step down from the original listing.The house continued to sit on the market. By the time it sold, the final price was much lower than both of the earlier asking prices.The Los Angeles Times reported that the property finally sold for $8.1 million in April 2019. That meant Williams accepted about $3.895 million less than the original $11.995 million asking price.On the basic purchase price alone, Williams still made money from the sale. She paid $6.612 million for the property in 2006 and sold it for $8.1 million in 2019.That puts the difference at about $1.488 million before expenses linked to the sale, such as commissions, taxes and other closing costs. So the $8.1 million transaction was not a loss compared with her original purchase price.At the same time, the final sale was far below the number Serena Williams had hoped to get when she first listed the home. The gap between the initial asking price and the final sale price was close to $3.9 million.For a property that stayed with Williams for about 13 years, the final deal therefore tells two different parts of the story: she did not get close to the original $12 million target, but she also sold the estate for more than she had paid for it.The Bel-Air sale closed a long chapter in Williams’ Los Angeles real estate history. The 2.7-acre property had been part of her life since 2006, but after her family grew and her housing plans changed, the older estate was eventually sold for $8.1 million.
Article Summary: Serena Williams sold her long-held Bel-Air estate for $8.1 million in April 2019. The tennis star bought the property in 2006 for $6.612 million and first listed it in late 2017 for $11.995 million. The 1935-built home sits on about 2.7 acres and has 6,101 square feet of living space, six bedrooms and seven bathrooms.

Article Title: “Pleased to be able to provide meaningful assistance to the students”: How Usain Bolt is helping Jamaican students after Hurricane Melissa as his foundation commits nearly J$10M
Article Text:
How Usain Bolt is helping Jamaican students after Hurricane Melissa as his foundation commits nearly J$10M(Getty Images)

Usain Bolt Foundation puts J$9.7M behind students across western Jamaica

How Usain Bolt is continuing his connection with Waldensia Primary School

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For families still recovering from Hurricane Melissa, school costs can add another burden. Usain Bolt is now helping Jamaican students whose families continue to deal with the storm’s impact.On Wednesday, the Usain Bolt Foundation announced nearly J$10 million in education support for more than 100 students entering secondary school. The assistance will cover school fees and other education-related expenses throughout the 2026-27 academic year.The initiative covers students from Trelawny, St. James, Hanover, Westmoreland and St. Elizabeth. Eight high schools have partnered with the foundation, with each school receiving J$1 million to support students facing financial difficulties.The schools include St. Elizabeth Technical High School and Maggoty High School in St. Elizabeth; Godfrey Stewart High School and Petersfield High School in Westmoreland; Green Island High School and Merlene Ottey High School in Hanover; and Green Pond High School and Maldon High School in St. James.Guidance counsellors at the participating schools will identify the students with the greatest financial needs.That allows the money to reach families who need help with school expenses while they recover from the hurricane.The Caribbean National Weekly article states that Usain Bolt was “pleased to be able to provide meaningful assistance to the students, particularly given the impact Hurricane Melissa had on their families and communities.”That support also extends to students from Bolt’s former school, making the programme more personal for the Jamaican sprint legend.Usain Bolt began his own education at Waldensia Primary School in Trelawny, and his foundation has continued to support students from the school.Under the latest initiative, all 17 Waldensia students who successfully completed their Primary Exit Profile examinations will receive J$100,000 each. The grants total J$1.7 million and bring the foundation’s overall commitment under the programme to J$9.7 million.The latest support follows another donation earlier in 2026. The Usain Bolt Foundation gave J$1.7 million to graduates of Waldensia Primary, extending its longstanding relationship with the school.Winsome Wilkins, chairman of the Usain Bolt Foundation, also highlighted the wider purpose behind the initiative. The Caribbean National Weekly report said Wilkins described the foundation’s mission as “creating a legacy of happy children” by enhancing their lives through educational and cultural development and inspiring young people to pursue their dreams.Education and youth development have remained central to the foundation’s charitable work. Now, that support reaches beyond Usain Bolt’s former school and into eight high schools across western Jamaica.For the more than 100 students receiving assistance, the J$9.7 million commitment can help reduce the cost of starting secondary school while their families continue recovering from Hurricane Melissa.For Usain Bolt, the latest move also shows how his foundation continues to turn his success on the track into opportunities for young Jamaicans. With students across five parishes now receiving help, the programme gives children a chance to focus on their next step in education while their families work through the challenges left by the hurricane.
Article Summary: Usain Bolt Foundation announces nearly J$10 million in education support for more than 100 students entering secondary school. The initiative covers students from Trelawny, St. James, Hanover, Westmoreland and St. Elizabeth. Eight high schools have partnered with the foundation, with each school receiving J$1 million.

Article Title: 62.5 lakh draft SIR voters flagged for anomalies, 59.7 lakh unmapped in Maharashtra
Article Text:
The SIR drive in Shivajinagar constituency





PUNE: Amravati’s Badnera (1.23 lakh), Pune’s Hadapsar (1.22 lakh), Thane’s Ovala Majiwada (1.18 lakh) and Mumbai’s Malad West (1.11 lakh) are among the 15 assembly constituencies in Maharashtra with the maximum discrepancies in the SIR list.Interestingly voters in three constituencies in Nagpur are set to receive over a lakh notices, including Nagpur North (1.08 lakh), Nagpur East (1.07 lakh) and Nagpur West (1.07 lakh).Notices are being issued to voters whose forms were not mapped to the earlier electoral roll as well as those whose enumeration forms reported anomalies or discrepancies (details including name, age, address) compared to those on the electoral roll.The assembly constituency of Badnera in Amravati has reported 1.08 lakh voters with anomalies, the highest in the state.The other constituencies with a large number of voters with anomalies include Kamthi in Nagpur (66,964), Nagpur North (61,248), Nalasopara in Palghar (55,875), Solapur South (50,978) and Malad West (49,703).The Nalasopara constituency has reported 1.04 lakh unmapped electors, highest in the state.This is followed by Hadapsar in Pune (85,853), Thane’s Ovala Majiwada (75,808) and Kalyan rural (71,544), Pune’s Khadakwasala (65,708) and Thane’s Airoli (65,180).Across the state, 62.5 lakh electors on the draft SIR roll have been reported with anomalies and 59.7 lakh are unmapped.Experts said the concentration in urban and rapidly expanding belts reflects higher population mobility and address changes, and expanding areas are witnessing a large number of unmapped voters, especially in the urban pockets.So far, 2 crore voters in the state were excluded in the SIR draft roll. Now another 1.2 crore voters will receive notices for documents and face scrutiny. As a result, the number of exclusions may increase.Electors on the draft list who will receive notices because their forms are unmapped or have anomalies, will have until Oct 29 to respond and provide the documents.Those in the unmapped category will have to provide proof of themselves or their relatives being part of the 2002-04 electoral roll through one of the 11 documents listed by the Election Commission of India. The final electoral roll of the SIR in the state will be published on Nov 4.A senior election official said the process of submitting documents addressing anomalies has been made simpler. BLOs have been told to collect required documents but voters can upload them online through the CEO website.They can log in using the EPIC number or notice reference number, receive an OTP on their registered cellphone number and upload the documents.
Article Summary: Badnera in Amravati has reported 1.08 lakh voters with anomalies, the highest in the state. The Nalasopara constituency in Palghar reports 1.04 lakh unmapped electors. Nagpur North, Nagpur East and Nagpur West are set to receive over a lakh notices.

Article Title: NLSIU ends uncertainty, to hold convocation on Oct 17
Article Text:
The National Law School of India University, located in Bengaluru, is set to hold its much-anticipated convocation on October 17.





BENGALURU: After a huge uproar in Aug and Sept over inviting the Chief Justice of India as chief guest, the off-again-on-again convocation of National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, will be held on Oct 17.However, the university did not explicitly state whether CJI will be officially present at the convocation. Sources claimed the CJI is keen to attend it.NLSIU had cancelled its convocation scheduled for Sept 12 amid a controversy over the participation of CJI and Bar Council of India chief.The standoff erupted after the graduating batch of NLSIU extended support to Hyderabad’s Nalsar students and expressed discontent in having CJI and Bar Council chief attending their convocation.At a meeting on Wednesday, the varsity’s executive council and general council discussed a proposal to hold the 34th annual convocation in Oct.The councils, “chaired by the hon’ble Chief Justice of India in his capacity as Chancellor of the University, approved the proposal and resolved to hold the 34th Annual Convocation on October 17,” said a mail from the university to the students.“The executive council and the general council approved the proposal,” said a mail from the university to the students.The alumni association is learnt to have played a major role in bringing a turnaround.The governing board of Alumni Association of the National Law School of India University, in a letter, explained how it has been engaging in dialogue with NLS and other stakeholders, including the CJI, for holding the convocation. This was acknowledged by the varsity.“During meetings with the CJI, (alumni) office-bearers were received with warmth and accorded a cordial and attentive audience. There was a shared recognition that the larger interests, aspirations, and legitimate expectations of the graduating students must remain paramount,” the association said.The governing bodies resolved that all graduating students would be formally conferred their degrees, either in person or in absentia, on the day.NLSIU has asked graduating students to intimate their choice of receiving their degrees and annulled all earlier notifications relating to the process of awarding degrees.The alumni association held discussions with graduating students across programmes to gauge their views on the convocation.“The overwhelming sentiment is that conferring degrees at a formal convocation carries considerable significance for them and their families. This had been conveyed to the CJI,” the association said.The AA thanked the NLSIU administration, the student cohort and the wider alumni community for their cooperation.
Article Summary: NLSIU had cancelled its convocation scheduled for Sept 12 amid a controversy over the participation of CJI and Bar Council of India chief. The standoff erupted after the graduating batch of NLSIU extended support to Hyderabad’s Nalsar students.

Article Title: Analogue alarm: How synthetic paneer takes a Gondola ride to your plate
Article Text:
Synthetic paneer production continues in Gondola village despite a statewide ban.

Synthetic paneer floods Delhi-NCR markets

Who Are The Buyers?

Is There A Health Impact?





Standing outside a closed gate that looks like the entrance to a foundry, the man who identifies himself as Imran asks what we want.“Paneer,” we say. “Do you take large orders?”“Any quantity,” he replies. “We supply to many places in Delhi, Gurgaon and Faridabad. Within a day, we can supply as much paneer as required to Chandigarh.”Imran wasn’t exaggerating. There would be few lives in Delhi-NCR and the vast agglomeration of towns and villages around it that the foundry-like units operating in a cluster here – Gondola village in Nuh’s Punahana block – would not have touched. Their chief produce – synthetic paneer (also analogue or non-dairy) is cheap, lasts a long time, and needs no dairy.Daily, synthetic paneer is delivered in bulk to distributors, mandis, and catering kitchens associated with banquet halls. On the plate, it comes packed into tikkas and stuffed in patties, kulchas, rolls and parathas, and in curries that are lapped up in massive quantities.Synthetic paneer (also analogue or non-dairy) is everywhere. Gondola is among its chief contributors. Last month, Haryana govt banned all forms of non-dairy paneer after finding their presence in a large number of samples tested at labs.But the units that bulk-produce paneer doppelgangers continue to churn out massive batches as orders flow in. The only difference? Gates are shut, and there’s a watch posted outside, just in case a nosy visitor drops by.“Food safety teams are active in the area,” says Imran. At another unit in Punahana city, workers turned abusive when we inquired about paneer production.Gondola specialises in all forms of synthetic paneer, like skimmed milk with palm oil and vegetable fats and soya paste treated mixed milk solids. Over the years, demand for cheap paneer has seen manufacturing units proliferate beyond a single cluster to Katpuri, Punahana city, Bara Bazidpur in Pinangwan, Raniyala and Bodi Kothi in Ferozepur Jhirka and Sheikhpur in Nagina, among other places.They produce quickly, and evidently, do whatever it takes to make their product look the best. “During recent raids on paneer manufacturing units in Punahana, food safety officials found buckets of slaked lime (chuna), which were being used to artificially whiten synthetic paneer,” said a food department source. A ballpark estimate of how much paneer the Gondola belt sends out daily, according to various officials and distributors, these correspondents spoke to, is around 10,000-12,000 kg.Haryana food safety commissioner Manoj Kumar has issued a one-year statewide prohibition under Section 30(2)(a) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, covering analogue or non-dairy paneer, and barring its preparation using milk powder or vegetable oil. Officials have been instructed to seize stocks and initiate criminal prosecution under the FSS Act.Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat, too, have banned synthetic paneer for a year. Sale and production of analogue paneer is not illegal in India as long as it is correctly labelled, but concerns about poor standards and the impact on health have led to a rethink.The state’s latest testing data underlines the scale of the problem: of 285 paneer samples tested between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026, 200 failed to meet standards. In many samples, the Butyrorefractometer (which measures purity) readings and iodine values were significantly beyond limits, showing replacement of natural milk fat with non-milk vegetable fats.Food delivery aggregator platforms are acting too. On Aug 31, Zomato announced a zero-tolerance policy on analogue dishes across its platform. It said restaurant partners have been asked to transition to natural dairy products, remove analogue-dairy items where an immediate switch isn’t feasible, and review supplier product labels and ingredient declarations to ensure accurate menu representation.“Thirteen paneer dairies have been proceeded against by the Nuh regional office. Out of these, three units have already been closed, closure orders have been received against five units, four units are presently under show cause notice, and closure recommendation against one sent to head office,” Nuh deputy commissioner Akhil Pilani said.A supplier described an organised distribution network connecting Nuh’s manufacturing units with Delhi-NCR’s catering and food businesses. Vehicles, he said, leave early morning carrying “freshly prepared synthetic paneer” to Delhi, Gurgaon and surrounding areas. The economics make the case for synthetic paneer. A commercial buyer paying Rs 340 for a kilogram of full-cream paneer could instead procure the cheapest variety (soya paste and vegetable oils, perhaps with a chuna whitener) for Rs 120-150. For a catering order of 1,000kg, this is a savings of Rs 2 lakh.Sources told TOI synthetic paneer is delivered to distributors at Khandsa Mandi, Subzi Mandi on Gurdwara Road, and Anaj Mandi in Gurgaon and at Janakpuri, Uttam Nagar, and in the east in Delhi, mostly for banquet halls, cloud kitchens and local dairy shops. Hapur, Palwal and Bhiwadi are other centres that produce synthetic paneer for supply to Delhi-NCR.Chef Sunnyy Vyas, also known as Brown Chef India, said texture and taste can offer clues, though they’re no substitute for lab testing. “After spending years in kitchens, you develop an instinct with ingredients,” he said. Good, fresh paneer should break softly and crumble rather than stretch like cheese or rubber, he explained — it typically has a soft, slightly grainy, milky feel and a fresh, milky flavour, whereas analogue products can feel unusually smooth, tight or rubbery, and taste more elastic or processed.But he cautioned this isn’t foolproof. “Some products are made very well and can be difficult to identify without checking the ingredients or doing a proper test.” His message for restaurants using analogue products was simple — transparency. “If they’re using analogue paneer, it should be mentioned clearly on the menu, preferably with the ingredients or what it is made from in brackets.”Paediatric endocrinologist Dr Ganesh Jevalikar said the concern goes beyond analogue paneer simply being different from the conventional dairy product. “Paneer is commonly consumed as an important source of protein, particularly by vegetarians, but analogue paneer can be deficient in protein because its preparation is fundamentally different and may rely on vegetable fats, palm oil, starches and emulsifiers,” he said.Regular consumption of products high in saturated fat, he added, could contribute to weight gain, obesity and increased LDL cholesterol, with longer-term risks including insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, particularly when eaten frequently. “The bigger issue is that a low-cost substitute should not be mistaken for a nutritionally equivalent food.”Surabhi Sharma, clinical nutritionist and dietetics at Max Hospital, Gurgaon, said: “The health impact depends on the formulation, serving size and frequency of consumption. Some analogue products can be higher in saturated fat, refined starch, calories and sodium, and lower in protein and calcium than regular dairy paneer. Consistently consuming such foods may therefore result in poorer overall nutrition. There is no scientific proof that properly controlled analogue paneer causes hormonal imbalance, so there is no need for unnecessary panic.”Manpreet Singh, honorary treasurer of National Restaurant Association of India, said good restaurants don’t serve analogue paneer because “that’s against the grain of the business”. “We had a talk organized by FSSAI a few days ago to teach restaurant owners how to maintain standards. Analogue paneer was also discussed, and according to law, you have to state it is analogue. When you’re a decent restaurant, you are charging a particular price. When you’re selling something for Rs 600, you don’t want to save that Rs 50.”
Article Summary: Synthetic paneer is cheap, lasts a long time, and needs no dairy. Haryana govt banned all forms of non-dairy paneer last month. But units that bulk-produce paneer doppelgangers continue to churn out massive batches.

Article Title: Outsiders spotted at office, full Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority unit shunted
Article Text:
The Social Development Branch handles the sensitive process of rehabilitation and resettlement of people affected by MMRDA’s infrastructure projects, including Metro projects





MUMBAI: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has ordered a wholesale change of its Social Development Branch, transferring all 16 officials and employees — from the deputy collector to peons — after Metropolitan commissioner Sanjay Mukherjee’s surprise inspection of the unit handling rehabilitation and housing for project-affected people (PAPs) .The move follows the detection of procedural lapses and the presence of unauthorised persons on the branch premises by Mukherjee during his inspection.He subsequently directed officials to undertake a detailed review of the branch’s functioning and strengthen administrative supervision and controls.Following the review, MMRDA decided to undertake a complete administrative restructuring of the branch.Employees working at different levels have been transferred and fresh responsibilities assigned for handling PAP cases, maintaining records, scrutinising applications and processing cases for further action.The deputy collector handling PAP-related matters, including cases linked to Metro projects, has also been transferred as part of the reshuffle.The branch plays a crucial role in facilitating rehabilitation housing for people displaced or affected by major infrastructure projects.It also processes applications and related documentation of eligible PAPs before allotment and other rehabilitation measures are undertaken.Given the sensitivity of PAP-related matters, the MMRDA administration has stressed the need for the process to remain transparent, properly documented and free from intermediaries.The presence of unauthorised persons in such a unit has therefore prompted the authority to tighten oversight.The wholesale transfers are being viewed as a significant administrative intervention aimed at strengthening accountability and ensuring that project-affected families get a more transparent and direct mechanism for pursuing their rehabilitation claims.
Article Summary: The Social Development Branch handles the sensitive process of rehabilitation and resettlement of people affected by MMRDA’s infrastructure projects. The move follows the detection of procedural lapses and the presence of unauthorised persons on the branch premises by Metropolitan commissioner Sanjay Mukherjee.

Article Title: Satya Niketan collapse fallout: 52 buildings with illegal 5th floor identified, could be razed
Article Text:
MCD commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar has stressed on instructions to act against the ongoing illegal construction, following the CM’s direction.





NEW DELHI: MCD Wednesday intensified its crackdown on unauthorised, ongoing or recently constructed fifth-floors, days after the Satya Niketan building collapse.Seven buildings with fifth floors under construction in violation of norms were identified in the Najafgarh zone alone and seven in Keshavpuram zone, according to MCD. In total, 52 such buildings identified in 12 zones and are being served notices.A senior MCD official said demolition at these properties could begin after a prescribed notice period. “Notices for unauthorised construction are first served, giving the owner a week to take corrective action. Thereafter, a demolition order is issued and action can be taken after another two weeks,” the official said.The building departments of all 12 zones have been directed to identify structures that violate height norms under the Unified Building Bye-Laws and MPD rules and serve notices to defaulters. “Enforcement (of rules) against such structures will be intensified,” an MCD official said.MCD commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar Tuesday stressed on instructions to act against the ongoing illegal construction, including unauthorised fifth-floor additions, following the chief minister’s direction.The civic body also continued its drive against dangerous and unauthorised structures. On Wednesday, it carried out 46 demolition actions across all 12 zones.In addition, 20 properties were sealed, 24 show-cause notices issued and 31 demolition/sealing orders passed.In Kucha Chelan, Jama Masjid, two roof panels at the ground-floor level and a partition wall were demolished with assistance from the Jama Masjid police station. Similar action was taken against an unauthorised construction at a property in Bazar Sitaram under the Sadar Paharganj zone.In Najafgarh, enforcement action was taken against properties declared dangerous in Vikas Nagar and Sector 17, Dwarka.In Keshavpuram zone, demolition was carried out on a property in Rana Pratap Bagh, covering all floors. At another property in Model Town, three RCC slab panels were demolished and the reinforcement was cut using a gas cutter for violating building norms.“The drive against unauthorised construction, misuse of properties and dangerous structures will be further intensified in the coming days,” officials said.MCD also continued demolition work at building number 13 in Satya Niketan, next to the building that collapsed on Sept 6.The civic body has identified 1,243 buildings which operate as paying guest (PG) facilities. These house around 24,000 occupants.
Article Summary: MCD intensified its crackdown on unauthorised, ongoing or recently constructed fifth-floors. Seven buildings with fifth floors under construction in violation of norms were identified in the Najafgarh zone alone. 52 such buildings identified in 12 zones and are being served notices.

Article Title: From chatbot to counsellor: AI now nudges young in distress to helplines
Article Text:
Counsellors say that 20% of calls follow AI prompts





AHMEDABAD: Anokhi (name changed), 22, a fresh IT engineering graduate, turned to a popular AI platform to make sense of what her physical signs—weight loss, lack of sleep and appetite, and constant stress—could mean.The conversation moved to her struggle to settle in a new city for work and the emotional fallout of ending a three-year relationship and starting a new one with a colleague.“When she called our helpline, she was a potential candidate for potential harm. She told us that the chatbot suggested the numbers to dial in case of distress. The counselling lasted for over an hour as she poured her heart out to discuss her aspirations and weight of parents’ dreams along with her personal life,” said Dr Shikha Talati, a psychiatrist and coordinator associated with TeleMANAS helpline (14416), a project by NIMHANS.“Timely intervention was provided as she is now in regular therapy and leading a healthy life.”Mental health professionals staffing suicide prevention and counselling helplines say such AI-to-human escalation is showing up more often, with people increasingly using chat-based tools to articulate distress and then being directed—by prompts or searches—to call a helpline.At TeleMANAS, Dr Talati said the service handles an average of 50-60 calls per month related to extreme depression and suicidal tendencies.Jeevan Aastha (1800-233-3330) is also seeing a noticeable share of callers arriving via AI-led discovery.Sanjivani Adhvaryu, a psychologist and senior mental health counsellor with the helpline, said that 20% of the average 40 to 50 daily calls made to the helpline were prompted by AI search.Experts say the trend of the young freely chatting with AI about mental health issues has made AI central to making mental health information and support more accessible.“But it is a deeply personal journey, and technology cannot replace the human touch,” Adhvaryu said.“Sometimes the chats are not to seek definite answers but just to pour heart out and to feel seen without judgement. We thus advise callers when needed for intervention by experts.”Counsellors say call patterns continue to reflect age-linked stressors. Analysis of Jeevan Aastha calls—about 1,200 per month—indicates younger callers more often cite interpersonal and relationship issues, middle-aged callers flag financial distress, and many elderly callers speak about health concerns and loneliness.September 10 is observed as World Suicide Prevention Day to create awareness about the issue. This year’s theme is ‘Changing the Narrative on Suicide’ with the call to action ‘Start the Conversation’.
Article Summary: Mental health professionals staffing suicide prevention and counselling helplines say such AI-to-human escalation is showing up more often. September 10 is observed as World Suicide Prevention Day to create awareness about the issue. This year’s theme is ‘Changing the Narrative on Suicide’ with the call to action ‘Start the Conversation’
